subject: warfarin
correct: BNF/BSH: INR 5–8 no bleeding: withhold 1–2 doses and reduce maintenance; INR >8 no bleeding: stop warfarin, oral vitamin K 1–5 mg, repeat if INR still high at 24 h; minor bleeding with INR >5: IV vitamin K 1–3 mg; major bleeding at ANY INR: stop, IV vitamin K 5 mg + prothrombin complex concentrate (hospital)
source: https://medibuddy.co.uk/?p=21057 (BNF/BSH warfarin reversal summary); BNF 'Coumarins and phenindione' treatment summary

fixes.old: INR >5.0 + bleeding → vitamin K + hospital.
fixes.new: INR 5–8, no bleeding → withhold 1–2 doses and reduce dose; INR >8 → oral vitamin K 1–5 mg; major bleeding at any INR → hospital (IV vitamin K + PCC) (BNF/BSH).

fixes.old: INR >4.0 → hold + recheck. INR >5 + bleeding → Vit K + hospital.
fixes.new: INR >4.0 → hold + recheck. INR 5–8 (no bleeding) → withhold 1–2 doses; INR >8 → oral vit K 1–5 mg; major bleeding at any INR → hospital (IV vit K + PCC).

fixes.old: INR >4 → hold + recheck 24h. INR >5 + bleeding → Vit K + hospital.
fixes.new: INR >4 → hold + recheck 24h. INR 5–8 (no bleeding) → withhold 1–2 doses; INR >8 → oral vit K 1–5 mg; major bleeding at any INR → hospital (IV vit K + PCC).

note: 'INR >5 + bleeding → vitamin K + hospital' implies a bleeding patient with INR <5 needs no escalation (major bleeding needs hospital at any INR) and omits the INR >8 no-bleeding oral vitamin K step. The 'INR >4 hold' local rule is left in place. TTR <65% (NICE NG196 poor control) vs TTR <60% (HAS-BLED labile INR) is legitimate.

subject: calcium
correct: Site/SfE-consistent triage: adjusted Ca ≥3.5, or symptomatic → emergency; 3.0–3.4 → same-day; 2.6–3.0 asymptomatic → repeat and investigate (PTH; NICE NG132)

fixes.old: Hypercalcaemia >2.8 or symptomatic → IV fluids (0.9% saline 3–6 L/24h), stop thiazide diuretics, bisphosphonates if malignancy-related (zoledronic acid 4mg IV), investigate cause (PTH, vitamin D, myeloma screen, CXR). Mild hypercalcaemia (<2.8) → recheck in 1 week, stop vitamin D supplements, hydrate.
fixes.new: Hypercalcaemia ≥3.5, or symptomatic (confusion, vomiting, dehydration) at any level → same-day hospital assessment for IV fluids ± bisphosphonate. 3.0–3.4 → same-day discussion. Asymptomatic 2.6–3.0 → repeat, check PTH (NICE NG132), review thiazides/calcium/vitamin D, myeloma screen and CXR as indicated.

fixes.old: Corrected Ca >2.65 mmol/L: check PTH, renal function, vitamin D;
fixes.new: Adjusted Ca ≥2.6 mmol/L (repeat to confirm): check PTH, renal function, vitamin D (NICE NG132);

note: '>2.8 → IV fluids 3–6 L/24h' gives a hospital regimen at a threshold used nowhere else on the site. Also cases/depression.html 'Corrected Ca >2.65 mmol/L: check PTH' could become '≥2.6 mmol/L (on two occasions, NICE NG132)' — included below.
